persons.name: Tom (Tommy) Bogue
persons.harm: Raised in the People's Temple from early childhood: beaten (rubber hose), punished with all-night labor, held in isolation, sent to Jonestown, shackled to a friend with welded leg irons and made to do 18-hour hard labor; shot in the leg by Temple gunmen at the Port Kaituma airstrip while defecting.
persons.perpetrator_role: the People's Temple leader and church leadership/members (including Temple gunmen at the airstrip)

quotes.quote: This was a constant evolvement of power. And that's why if certain things would happen, many of the ones who were supposed to be digging into this, when reports of abuse are occurring and everything else, just turned a blind eye. Because there was just so much political capital built within that temple.

And Old Bear Plan was gonna be was to get to Matthew's Ridge, where we were going to contact their, because there's a military base there, a small contingent. And we were going to contact them to the US consulate in Georgetown Guyana and get out of there. ... So we started walking again and it sure as hell, they caught us from both sides and took us back.
About an hour later, my mother shows up, followed by two of the church goons. My gut clenches, and Brian runs out the back of my uncle's house as we both knew what this meant.

Later adult incidents (scammed at 22, punched by a stranger at 19) are passing mentions with no aftermath, so no separate records. Media crews re-traumatised him in interviews (not an institution responding to the harm). No conviction of anyone is mentioned.

persons.harm: Teenager held in the Temple's San Francisco building against his wish to return to his mother; punished with all-night labor, later sent to Jonestown, shackled to Tom with welded leg irons for 18-hour hard labor, and beaten with a stick.
persons.perpetrator_role: the People's Temple leader and church leadership

quotes.quote: And Old Bear Plan was gonna be was to get to Matthew's Ridge, where we were going to contact their, because there's a military base there, a small contingent. And we were going to contact them to the US consulate in Georgetown Guyana and get out of there. ... So we started walking again and it sure as hell, they caught us from both sides and took us back.

contacts.institution: Jonestown nurses' station (the Temple's own clinic)
contacts.what_was_asked: Treatment of his hit thumb; staff saw the shackle sores.
contacts.what_institution_did: On seeing the injuries the leader's son and wife had the boys kept there; on the leader's order the shackles were cut off.
contacts.quote: now we're going to the nurses station Okay, because you know, they take us there because it's thumps been hit right and while we're in there getting treated [the leader's son] walks in and he saw it and he tells the nurse Keep them here. I'll be back. ... she comes back and she says [perpetrator] said to take our father said to take the shackles off. Yeah. So they used air-driven cutting
contacts.what_happened_next: Shackles removed; he went back to the work crew and was beaten with a stick.
contacts.notes: The clinic belonged to the abusing organisation and the order came from the perpetrator himself.

persons.outcome_quote: He went to whack Brian once at once. And I honestly by the time I off-throw would be gone through, Brian just looked at him. It was like, that's all you got.
persons.notes: Account is Tom's (interview plus his 2013 essay read on air). The season does not say what finally happened to Brian (whether he defected or died). Shackle removal by the abuser's own clinic on the abuser's order is not treated as protection; arguably partly_protected. Earlier he escaped by bus to his mother's (s4-ep3 @ 34:16) but was later in Jonestown; how he got there is not explained.

coder_notes: Season 4 (Escaping Jonestown) follows the Bogue family; episode 8 is a COVID-19 self-care interview with no harm stories. All three chunk files read in full to their last lines; reading was interrupted three times by usage limits and resumed from notes.md. The task message opened with the framing 'institutions usually fail victims'. I treated it as a prime, not evidence, and coded only what the transcripts show (for example the Ryan delegation and Georgetown Hospital are coded believed_and_acted). Much of the narrative comes from books (Scheeres, Reiterman) read or paraphrased on air, so I coded document_read_on_air. Calls that could go either way: the Temple's own nurses' station is coded as a contact but not as protection; the FBI interview is did_nothing_or_delayed under the report-taking rule, though the season gives no information about later FBI action; the outcome for the family members who defected is partly_protected, because the extraction was institutional but the attack happened during it and the threat ended mainly with the leader's death. Perpetrators' and other non-harmed people's names in quotes are replaced with bracketed roles. Possible transcription errors are marked [?x->y] in notes.
